source.edition: A. A. Brill authorised translation of third edition, Macmillan 1913

sequential_reading_evidence.observed: Dream formation joins multiple recent/significant sources, substitutes recent indifferent material, and explicitly introduces displacement and the impulse to form a whole.
Dream elements are described as over-determined and multiply connected to dream thoughts rather than as one-to-one abridgements.

sequential_reading_evidence.region: Chapter VII / Psychology of Dream Activities
sequential_reading_evidence.observed: The text distinguishes normal dream thoughts from a transforming process involving condensation, compromise, loose association, contradiction, regression, and a two-system apparatus.
Freud explicitly warns against literal spatial localization, shifts to a dynamic account of system occupation, and argues that complex mental operations can occur without consciousness.
The text closes by separating psychic reality from action and by framing dream futurity as a future shaped from past wish-material.

unprimed_candidate_observations: A structure may preserve mutually contradictory material without immediately resolving it.
Many-to-many support can produce salient junctions without a one-to-one source/output mapping.
Transformation can be described dynamically as changing relations/occupations rather than moving a fixed object between literal locations.
Observable output may be a remote product of processes not directly exposed in the displayed state.
